data.name: Final Cut: Homage Collector's Edition
data.detailed_description:
From the developers who brought you the Hidden Expedition series

…Eipix’s dramatic continuation of the Final Cut story line! A serial killer calling himself “the Director” has targeted your father’s movie legacy for his magnum opus, and he’s cast you in the starring role.

Your father’s projector appears again as a game-play feature, allowing you to switch between real-life scenes and the Director’s movie sets. Save your family from certain death as the Director tries to immortalize them as works of “art.” Beat him at his game of cat-and-mouse. And uncover the Director’s true identity before the final credits roll!

This is a special Collector's Edition release full of exclusive extras you won’t find in the standard version. The Collector’s Edition includes:

Play role-reversal as the detective in the bonus game!
Collect old-school clapperboards hidden throughout the game
Use the available Strategy Guide
Win cool achievements
Get wallpapers, concept art, and soundtracks

reviews.review:
This third installment was nowhere near as fun a game as the first and second games. The second was the best of the series so far. This game had a very stupid and predictable story. Some bad guy calling himself The Director is inspired to commit murder and calls it art. Yep, haven't heard that one before. We are treated to a bunch of recordings of this godawful community college acting major spouting nonsense with this forced sinister sneer in his voice. It was so obvious who he was from the very beginning. The dialogue seemed to be written by the non-English speaking wing of Big Fish because some of the comments made by our heroine were inane and inappropriate at times. 
And the story itself was not well thought out. The murderer's goal was to tarnish the name of the great director Morton Wolf by framing his daughter for murder. However, his plan had absolutely nothing to do with Wolf beyond framing his daughter for a murder. How would that tarnish a great director's name when he's already been dead for years so is not around to see it? Even the way the guy was going to frame the daughter was stupid. Um, YOU are the one trespassing and had a gun on you. How did you think that was going to look like self defense? Did you think this through for even one second? Developers? Did ya? (tumbleweeds)

The puzzles were more difficult in this game compared to the previous game. I don't enjoy constant spinning puzzles and there were quite a few of those here. Spin the wheel and line up all the reds with the reds, greens with greens, etc. I don't enjoy those. but you might.  Even the HOP puzzles were not as fun because it was a lot of those interactive type where you just move things around or use the screwdriver to open the crate and that gets you the paperclip which you use to open the zipper. Those kind of HOPs instead of just giving you a list of things to find. I always viewed the HOPs as a break from the game in some way. Just a way to relax, look around, and click. But you really can't do that in this game because they were trying to be all things to all people. Bad call.
The map is shoddily made and requires too many clicks to see where things are. You have to click on a circle and it takes you to another circle, often with chains across it for some unknown reason. You can still get to that location so the chains are meaningless. No idea why they didn't just keep the map the way it was in the other games and every other casual game. Click map, it shows you places you can travel, and you click them. We're not reinventing the wheel here. Another thing that made no sense is the locations in NY. They put the ship harbor in the center of midtown Manhattan (and no it wasn't meant to be the Central Park marina) and the train station looked to be in the middle of the East River. Why not just make it a fake city if you don't know the geography of NY?

The strategy guide is all messed up too. Just shoddily put together. The morphing cheat sheet is all out of order and hard to follow. The game doesn't seem to want to help keep track of the collectibles so you have to count for yourself. The morphing objects are only in the HOP sections, so very easy to miss those. The tutorial doesn't even mention that there are collectibles so it's totally useless too. I don't think people need to be told how to click on items with a magnifying glass. But they DO need to be told when there are collectibles and morphing items. 

This game was a chore to finish. It was almost the game that made me want to stop playing these kinds of games. Something about it was just too predictable and the mini games too convoluted and just NOT FUN to play. Can't figure out why, but the game was just boring and hard to remain engaged.
Hoping the next game is better.
